Info.title: Proposed network
Info.desc: Physics-informed parametric operator network: sensor labels of the training boards plus the physics, steady-state and moment loss of the physics-only boards (standard and extended, h 250-5000 W/(m2K)); log-linear condition heads
Info._note: Edit the values only. Keys starting with '_' are comments and are ignored. 'CHANGE' marks parameters that depend on the computer (GPU memory, runtime); all other values are those of the paper.

Net._K: Space functions: number of space functions phi_k (trunk outputs) and time constants tau_k per chip
Net._width: Trunk width: neurons per hidden layer of the trunk network
Net._depth: Trunk depth: number of hidden layers of the trunk network
Net._nF: Fourier frequencies: Fourier frequencies per coordinate of the trunk input
Net._rel: Relative coordinates: (1): coordinates relative to every chip as trunk inputs, (0): absolute coordinates only
Net._tauCap: Maximum time constant: upper limit of the time constants: lambda_k >= 1/tauCap (s)
Net._lin: Log-linear condition heads: (1): log of the decay rates and of a gain of every space function get a linear term of the scaled condition (log h, log k_diel, ...) outside the tanh layers, i.e., they follow a power law of h beyond the training range instead of saturating; (0): off (base network)

Loss._alpha: Data weight: weight of the data loss (labels at the sensor nodes)
Loss._beta: Physics weight: weight of the physics loss (finite-volume residual of the physics-only boards; 0: no physics)
Loss._gamma: Steady-state weight: weight of the steady-state loss (sum of phi_k equals G^-1 Bp; 0: off)
Loss._phys: Physics-only boards: (1): use the physics-only boards (physics and steady-state loss), (0): labelled boards only
Loss._physSet: Physics set: physics-only boards of the physics, steady-state and moment loss: phys (h 500-5000 W/(m2K), labelled range), physExt (h 250-5000 W/(m2K), extended below the labels) or phys+physExt (both, 400 boards)
Loss._delta: Moment weight: weight of the moment loss, i.e., sum_k phi_k/lambda_k^j = (G^-1 C)^j G^-1 Bp for j = 1 ... nMom on every board (moments of the transfer function, dominated by the slow modes; constrains the time constants on the physics-only boards); 0: off
Loss._nMom: Moments: number of matched moments j = 1 ... nMom (the steady state j = 0 is the steady-state loss)

Train._epoch: maximum number of epochs; paper value, for a quick check of the chain use setup['epoch'] in the setup file instead
Train._pat: Patience: early stopping after pat epochs without improvement of the validation RMSE (at the sensors)
Train._nStep: Steps per epoch: optimiser steps per epoch
Train._lr: Learning rate: initial learning rate of Adam (halved after 5 epochs without improvement)
Train._clip: Gradient clipping: maximum norm of the gradient
Train._seed: CHANGE only for a repetition with another seed (spread of the results); paper: 42
Train._Ts: Sampling time: sampling time of the profiles (s)

Samp._nbD: Data boards per step: labelled profiles per optimiser step
Samp._nbP: CHANGE (GPU memory): physics-only boards per optimiser step; memory per step ~ nbP x chips x N x K
Samp._nR: CHANGE (GPU memory, runtime): nodes of the physics residual per board and step
Samp._nbS: Steady-state boards: boards per step of the steady-state loss
Samp._tP: Physics profile length: length of the random loss profiles of the physics loss (s)
Samp._holdMin: Minimum hold time: minimum hold time of the random loss profiles of the physics loss (s)
Samp._holdMax: Maximum hold time: maximum hold time of the random loss profiles of the physics loss (s)
Samp._nCache: CHANGE (GPU memory): boards of the physics loss with G^-1 in memory; dense G^-1 needs 4 N^2 bytes per board (coarse N = 790: 2.5 MB, medium N = 3551: 50 MB, 16 boards 0.8 GB). Reduce if CUDA runs out of memory (the physics loss then sees fewer boards per epoch), increase on larger GPUs
Samp._nNew: Cache renewal: boards of the cache replaced per epoch
Samp._nDense: CHANGE (GPU memory): boards with more nodes keep only nR rows of G^-1 (sparse LU) instead of the dense inverse (8000: coarse and medium dense, fine rows) (nodes)

Mesh._note: values that replace the ones above on a mesh (coarse, medium, fine)

fine._nR: CHANGE (GPU memory): rows of G^-1 per cached board on the fine mesh (N = 21080: 2048 rows = 173 MB per board)
fine._nCache: CHANGE (GPU memory): cached boards on the fine mesh (8 x 173 MB = 1.4 GB); reduce on GPUs < 8 GB
fine._epoch: maximum number of epochs on the fine mesh; runtime ~115 s per epoch on an RTX 3070 (8 GB), i.e. ~3-5 h per run with early stopping
fine._pat: early-stopping patience on the fine mesh (epochs)
